text.p: Supermarket group Safeway Plc is planning to develop its joint venture with Fitzwilton Plc into a "powerful all-Ireland business", finance director Simon Laffin said on Thursday.
"We are currently actively seeking sites in the south (Irish Republic)," Laffin told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Laffin said the 50-50 venture, Safeway Stores (Ireland) Ltd, would aim to open three to four stores annually, "some in the north, but probably more in the south".
"We believe the local knowledge and experience of our partner will open doors," he added.

The joint venture will acquire nine stores and four sites from Fitzwilton for a total consideration of 65 million pounds. It will also take a further six stores under licence with options to purchase. All are in Northern Ireland.
Laffin said around 50 million stg would be spent on converting stores to the Safeway brand and upgrading them with the addition of facilities such as petrol stations, crches and dry cleaning.
The development of the four sites is expected to cost some 40 million stg while Laffin said the venture was likely to spend a further 40-50 million stg annually on new stores.
"This deal will allow us to open 19 stores in pretty short order in what is an under-served market," Laffin said.
Safeway has pledged to maintain the jobs of over 2,000 staff employed by Fitzwilton's Wellworth stores and create 1,000 new jobs through its four new supermarkets.
"We are looking for a substantial sales uplift so it should be good news on the job front," he said.

Laffin noted that Wellworth had managed to run a successful business during the 28-year conflict in Northern Ireland. He said the joint venture aimed to work with both sides of the community in the province.
